title: Probe Rotation and Eval Garden Manifest
author: Asha Patel
body:
Summary and intent:

This document defines the Eval Garden pattern and the Probe Rotation Manifest: a coordinated, budget-aware system for keeping probe sets (synthetic and production-derived) fresh, diverse, and locality-aware across shadow, dedicated, and private deployments. The goal is to make continuous evaluation resilient to drift, quantization artifacts, and configuration changes while minimizing cost and annotation overhead.

Goals:
- Ensure representative probes are exercised across all serving modes (hosted, dedicated, private) on a repeatable cadence.
- Maintain an auditable, versioned rotation policy for probes so that regressions are attributable and reproducible.
- Make the eval schedule locality- and workload-aware (per-customer slices, long-tail intents, and long-context interactions).
- Integrate quantization-awareness into probe selection so probes sensitive to numeric compression are prioritized pre-rollout.

High-level concepts:
- Eval Garden: a logical collection of probe beds (groups) that map to slices, regions, and model-variant compatibility. Examples: "assistant-core", "forms-extraction-longctx", "embeddings-english-high-similarity".
- Probe: an individual test item (prompt + context + expected checks). Probes can be synthetic, anonymized production traces, or human-curated edgecases.
- Probe Bed: a group of probes with shared scheduling rules and ownership.
- Rotation Policy: per-bed schedule describing cadence, retention, sampling strategy, and budget allocation.
- Probe TTL and Decay: probes age out to prioritize new coverage; decay controls probability of re-selection.

Architecture and components:
- Probe Registry (service): stores probe metadata, labels, signatures, provenance, and quant-sensitivity flags. Every probe has a stable id: PR-<sha1>.
- Gardener Scheduler: a policy engine that materializes rotation plans as yields for the Eval Runner. Supports locality constraints (region, tenant, model-variant).
- Eval Runner / Shadow Harness: executes probes against target endpoints (shadow, dedicated, private) and records telemetry to Eval Ingest.
- Eval Ingest / Metrics Pipeline: normalizes outputs, extracts token-level deltas, embedding-similarity logs, and checklist failures.
- Probe Monitor & Alerting: computes freshness, coverage, and regression scores; surfaces P0/P1 regressions and health trends.

Probe lifecycle (detailed):
1) Authoring: probes are authored via the Probe Registry UI or CLI. Every probe includes: text, seed context, deterministic RNG seed (optional), annotations (slices, sensitivity tags), and a quant-sensitivity score (0-1) produced by a quick local check.
2) Vetting: new probes run in a preflight bucket (30 runs across model seeds) to estimate variance and flakiness. Probes with high variance flagged as "unstable" and quarantined.
3) Assignment to Bed: owners assign probes to a Probe Bed and select Rotation Policy.
4) Rotation: the Gardener Scheduler selects probes for the next cycle respecting constraints: budget (token-cost cap), locality, minimum-bed-coverage, and probe TTL.
5) Execution: Eval Runner executes probes and sends normalized results.
6) Scoring & Archival: probes that exceed failure thresholds are promoted to triage workflows or archived if obsolete.

Rotation policy template (YAML example):

# rotation-policy.yaml
name: forms-extraction-longctx-rotation
bed_id: BED-forms-longctx
cadence: weekly            # daily | weekly | monthly | on-demand
budget_tokens_per_cycle: 200000   # gross token budget across all runs
min_bed_coverage: 90       # percent of probes to touch before reusing
locality_constraints: [eu-west-1, us-east-1]
quant_priority_threshold: 0.6   # probes with quant-sens >= this get 2x weight
sample_strategy: stratified_by_slice
decay_half_life_days: 21
max_runs_per_probe: 10
flaky_retest_policy: 3
owner: feature-forms-team

Scheduling rules (bulleted):
- If quant_priority_threshold triggers, schedule those probes earlier in the cycle and mark for per-quant-mode runs (e.g., 8-bit, mixed).
- Maintain at least one warmup run on a matched-cold-cache replica before taking samples used for production gating.
- Prefer probes that have not run in last TTL days until min_bed_coverage satisfied.
- Reserve 20% of budget for high-variance probes (flaky-retest pool).

ASCII table: (example cadence vs budget allocation)

| Cadence | Budget Tokens | Retention Window | Typical Bed Size | Notes |
| daily   | 50k           | 7 days           | 200-400 probes   | focused smoke & critical slices |
| weekly  | 200k          | 30 days          | 1k-3k probes     | broader coverage & quant-sensitivity |
| monthly | 800k          | 90 days          | 5k+ probes       | long-tail, multilingual sweep |

Telemetry and signal mapping:
- Per-probe outputs: response tokens, latency p50/p95/p99, failure checklist flags, embedding similarity vs gold (cosine), top-k log-prob delta, hallucination score (syntactic and factual heuristics).
- Derived signals: probe-failure-rate (30d EWMA), probe-flakiness-index, quant-degradation-index (per-quant-mode), slice-stability-score.
- Alerts: Team-level alerts fire when slice-stability-score drops > 6% in a week or quant-degradation-index crosses 0.15.

Alert thresholds (recommended):
- P0: any probe in "critical" slice that flips to incorrect output for 100% of runs across 3 seeds -> immediate pager.
- P1: slice-stability-score drop > 6% for 7d with absolute failure-rate > 2% -> Slack triage channel.
- P2: probe-flakiness-index > 0.4 for > 14d -> ticket to steward.

Runbook: responding to a failing rotation cycle (quick path):
1) Triage owner notified by PagerDuty (P0) or Slack (P1).
2) Escalation checklist:
   a) Confirm failing probe id and bed. Collect last 7 successful runs and diffs.
   b) Check model-variant and quant-mode combinator matrix for recent rollouts.
   c) Re-run failing probe in isolated environment with deterministic seed and verbose tracing enabled.
   d) If failure reproduces only under quantized modes, tag as QUANT-REGRESSION and follow the Quant Fallback policy.
3) If regression affects multiple beds or slices, trigger shadow-rollforward containment: revert traffic to previous model-variant or enable automatic fallback route.
4) Document triage outcome in the Probe Registry ticket and attach delta artifacts (tokens, traces, attribution).

Ownership and service-levels:
- Bed owner: maintains probe bed content, rotation policy, and acts as first responder for its alerts. (Examples: feature-forms-team, embeddings-core).
- Eval Platform: responsible for reliability of Gardener Scheduler, Eval Runner infra, and metrics pipeline. SLA: 99.9% job-scheduling success per cycle.
- Onboarding requirement: any model promotion to "production" must have passed 3 full rotation cycles across affected beds with quant-priority runs if applicable.

Model onboarding integration notes:
- As part of inference-readiness checks: require a rotation plan that includes at least one high-confidence probe bed exercised under the target quant-mode and a verification of embedding drift < 0.02 on representative slices.
- Shadow Promotion Gate: promotion requires no new P0s and less than 1% new slice regressions after 3 rotations.

Quantization-aware guidance:
- Tag probes with quant-sensitivity: run a small local quant-scan (reference tool: tools/quant-scan) that returns a sensitivity metric. Anything > 0.6 should be executed early and at increased sample count.
- Mixed precision and hybrid deployments should have separate probe-beds to isolate numeric-compression effects.

Operational examples (CLI):
- Register a probe: 
  rwd-probe register --file probe.json --bed BED-forms-longctx --owner feature-forms-team
- Schedule a one-off rotation run: 
  rwd-gardener run --bed BED-forms-longctx --mode on-demand --quant-modes 8bit,mix16
- Query probe health: 
  rwd-probe status --probe-id PR-1a2b3c --last 30d

Sample probe manifest (JSON; stored in Probe Registry):
{
  "id": "PR-1a2b3c",
  "bed": "BED-forms-longctx",
  "text": "Extract customer name from a 2-page receipt with overlapping OCR noise.",
  "context": "{page1:..., page2:...}",
  "owner": "feature-forms-team",
  "tags": ["long-context", "ocr-noise", "critical"],
  "quant_sensitivity": "0.72",
  "created": "2025-10-04"
}

Best practices and heuristics:
- Keep probes small but representative; long probes are expensive—split into anchored micro-probes when possible.
- Maintain explicit provenance: label origin (synthetic vs anon-prod) and the sampling policy used to create the probe.
- Annotate ownership and replacement criteria so beds can be rotated by non-authors after 90 days without re-approval.
- Use the flakiness pool to periodically re-evaluate and either stabilize or retire noisy probes.

Appendix: common failure modes and mitigations
- False-positive regressions due to tokenization drift: mitigation -> include tokenizer version/tag in run metadata and fail gating on stable-tokenizer runs only.
- Regression only under long-context: mitigation -> pre-warm KV cache and include warmup run to get stable performance baseline.
- Quantization-induced semantic drift: mitigation -> increase sample count for quant-sensitive probes and compare embedding-similarity profiles before gating.

References and links:
- See also: "probe-lifecycle" checklist (internal link), "quant-profile-synthesis-and-safety-playbook-2024" and "shadow-rollforward-and-mesh-simulation-playbook-2026" for rollback policies.
